data.note:
Dossier reflection - specimen s_5a98540349 cytochalasin B (PubChem CID 5311281, ChEMBL CHEMBL411729, no curated ChEMBL MoA, BBBC021 annotated Actin disruptors):

My conclusion Microtubule stabilizers 0.38 was incorrect. Correct is Actin disruptors.

**What I saw:** Strong dose-dependent tub_mean (z +1.29 at 0.03 µM → +6.65 at 0.3 µM → +7.45 at 1.0 µM → +27.7 at 10 µM, rho +1.0, e9), tub_std/glcm_contrast, act_mean/act_glcm_contrast, cell_area -7 to -12, frac_multinucleate_proxy +1.95 → +14.9 (rho +1.0, e10), nuc_solidity -18.4 and nuc_area -10.6 at high dose, flat frac_mitotic_like 0.0 and cell_count p=0.6 (e14). Visual: perinuclear tubulin rings/bundles, reduced spread.

**Why I was fooled:** I weighted early tubulin bundling with intact actin at 0.3 µM (e18, model called Microtubule stabilizers; tub_mean z=6.6 vs act_glcm z=1.8) and progressive multinucleation as antimitotic arrest, discounting the high-dose dominant actin signal (e6: act_glcm_contrast z=36.0, act_std z=18.7, act_mean z=16.5, actin punctate aggregates, tub compacted secondary to rounding). I under-weighted the atlas (e8: 0/10 Microtubule stabilizer neighbours, 5/10 Epithelial) and ignored that frac_mitotic_like never rose and cell_count flat argues against true mitotic block. Eg5/Aurora also produce multinucleation with normal tub increase (e18 uncertainty).

**Ground truth mechanism:** Cytochalasin B caps barbed ends of F-actin, blocking polymerization and shortening filaments (PMID 8204105) and altering actin assembly-dependent processes such as growth cone motility (PMID 1608453). This causes loss of stress fibers → cortical punctate aggregates (high act_glcm_contrast/std), cell rounding/shrinkage, failure of cytokinesis → dose-dependent binucleate/multinucleate accumulation (e10) and irregular nuclei (nuc_solidity rho -1.0, e12). Compacted rounded cells artifactually increase tubulin density/brightness and heterogeneity, mimicking a stabilizer. One well/dose made trends look cleaner than warra

reflection.text:
Unblinded truth is cytochalasin B, PubChem CID 5311281 - Actin disruptors. My two submissions were Microtubule stabilizers p=0.47 then p=0.38 - both wrong and over-confident.

What the evidence got right:
- High-dose quantitative profile correctly flagged Actin. Well w_b9f2cbcfb2 at 10 uM e3 had act_glcm_contrast z=+36.0 as the strongest feature, ahead of tub_mean z=+27.7 and tub_std z=+23.0, with dose_response rho=+1.00 for both act_glcm_contrast e13 and act_mean e15. Microscopist 1 on that well e6 gave candidates: Actin disruptors with 5 observations and density lower. That was the correct signal.
- Multinucleation/cytokinesis failure was real and dose-dependent: w_9c437e9416 at 1 uM e4 frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+8.4, dose_response rho=+1.00 e10, alongside cell_area z=-7.2 to -8.4 e2/e4 and cell_nuc_area_ratio z=-5.0 e2 and nuc_area rho=-1.00 e11 and nuc_solidity rho=-1.00 e12. This is classic for cytochalasin B actin filament capping/shortening PMID 8204105 leading to failed cleavage furrow, not specific to microtubule stabilization.
- Atlas correctly warned me: e8 0/10 Microtubule-stabilizer neighbours (5/10 Epithelial, 2/10 Cholesterol-lowering, 2/10 Protein synthesis). My hypotheses kept Microtubule stabilizers at 0.47 and 0.38 despite that direct contradiction.

What misled me and why:
- I over-weighted tub_mean. Low-mid dose w_f97f19f984 e2 tub_mean z=+6.6 at 0.3 uM, mid dose e4 +7.5, high dose e3 +27.7, with dose_response rho=+1.00 e9. I interpreted this as polymerization/bundling. In actin disruption this is a secondary measurement artifact: cell_area z=-7.2 to -8.4 indicates strong contraction/rounding, so tubulin intensity per area rises and compacted tubulin mimics bundled stabilizer signal. I treated a morphometric intensity increase as mechanistic polymerization without an in vitro tubulin assay.
- I treated shared phenotype as discriminative. Progressive multinucleation plus small irregular nuclei occurs in Actin disruptors, Microtubule stabilizers, and Aurora kinase inhibitors. The 1.0 uM microscopist e7 explicitly called Aurora kinase inhibitors and the high-dose call was Actin first, explicitly demoting stabilizers per review. I should have increased uncertainty instead of favoring stabilizers.
- Acquisition choice made this worse: I used budget on 4 wells with 1 well per dose e1, no replicates. All dose_response trends e9-e13 are 4 wells/4 doses with rho=+/-1.00 p=0 - mathematically perfect but biologically uninterpretable, as the review noted. cell_count rho=-0.40 p=0.6 e14 was flat and frac_mitotic_like was 0.0 throughout, which argues against classic stabilizer mitotic arrest, yet I discounted it.
- The requested 0.3 uM describe_phenotype e18 - 2 fields, density lower, 7 observations, candidates: Microtubule stabilizers - reinforced the wrong ranking. At earliest strong-effect dose with tub_mean +6.6 but act_glcm_contrast only +1.8, preserved actin stress fibres are expected early for cytochalasin B before high-dose punctate aggregates appear at 10 uM e3. I read preserved actin as evidence against actin disruptors, when it is consistent with dose progression.

Lookup e21/e22 confirmed name and BBBC021 structure agree for cytochalasin B but provided no curated mechanisms to rescue the inference, and literature search on actin disruptor multinucleation tubulin phenotype returned 0 hits e24, leaving me without orthogonal context.

Lesson: when actin texture is the strongest high-dose feature and atlas is 0/10 for the top call with conflicting microscopist calls across doses, a strong tubulin intensity dose-response should be down-weighted as secondary to cell contraction, and probability should stay near 0.25 or lower without replicate wells or a tubulin polymerization / actin filament direct assay.

e4/e10 multinucleation dose-dependent rho +1.00 is consistent with actin cytokinesis failure PMID 8204105
e8 atlas 0/10 stabilizer neighbours contradicted my call
e14 flat cell_count and persistent nuc_area/solidity -1.00 trends argued against stabilizer arrest
what_was_wrong: misinterpreted tub_mean +6.6 to +27.7 dose_response as stabilizer polymerization not compaction artifact from cell_area -7.2 to -8.4

## Reflection

Unblinded truth is cytochalasin B, PubChem CID 5311281 - Actin disruptors. My two submissions were Microtubule stabilizers p=0.47 then p=0.38 - both wrong and over-confident.

What the evidence got right:
- High-dose quantitative profile correctly flagged Actin. Well w_b9f2cbcfb2 at 10 uM e3 had act_glcm_contrast z=+36.0 as the strongest feature, ahead of tub_mean z=+27.7 and tub_std z=+23.0, with dose_response rho=+1.00 for both act_glcm_contrast e13 and act_mean e15. Microscopist 1 on that well e6 gave candidates: Actin disruptors with 5 observations and density lower. That was the correct signal.
- Multinucleation/cytokinesis failure was real and dose-dependent: w_9c437e9416 at 1 uM e4 frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+8.4, dose_response rho=+1.00 e10, alongside cell_area z=-7.2 to -8.4 e2/e4 and cell_nuc_area_ratio z=-5.0 e2 and nuc_area rho=-1.00 e11 and nuc_solidity rho=-1.00 e12. This is classic for cytochalasin B actin filament capping/shortening PMID 8204105 leading to failed cleavage furrow, not specific to microtubule stabilization.
- Atlas correctly warned me: e8 0/10 Microtubule-stabilizer neighbours (5/10 Epithelial, 2/10 Cholesterol-lowering, 2/10 Protein synthesis). My hypotheses kept Microtubule stabilizers at 0.47 and 0.38 despite that direct contradiction.

What misled me and why:
- I over-weighted tub_mean. Low-mid dose w_f97f19f984 e2 tub_mean z=+6.6 at 0.3 uM, mid dose e4 +7.5, high dose e3 +27.7, with dose_response rho=+1.00 e9. I interpreted this as polymerization/bundling. In actin disruption this is a secondary measurement artifact: cell_area z=-7.2 to -8.4 indicates strong contraction/rounding, so tubulin intensity per area rises and compacted tubulin mimics bundled stabilizer signal. I treated a morphometric intensity increase as mechanistic polymerization without an in vitro tubulin assay.
- I treated shared phenotype as discriminative. Progressive multinucleation plus small irregular nuclei occurs in Actin disruptors, Microtubule stabilizers, and Aurora kinase inhibitors. The 1.0 uM microscopist e7 explicitly called Aurora kinase inhibitors and the high-dose call was Actin first, explicitly demoting stabilizers per review. I should have increased uncertainty instead of favoring stabilizers.
- Acquisition choice made this worse: I used budget on 4 wells with 1 well per dose e1, no replicates. All dose_response trends e9-e13 are 4 wells/4 doses with rho=+/-1.00 p=0 - mathematically perfect but biologically uninterpretable, as the review noted. cell_count rho=-0.40 p=0.6 e14 was flat and frac_mitotic_like was 0.0 throughout, which argues against classic stabilizer mitotic arrest, yet I discounted it.
- The requested 0.3 uM describe_phenotype e18 - 2 fields, density lower, 7 observations, candidates: Microtubule stabilizers - reinforced the wrong ranking. At earliest strong-effect dose with tub_mean +6.6 but act_glcm_contrast only +1.8, preserved actin stress fibres are expected early for cytochalasin B before high-dose punctate aggregates appear at 10 uM e3. I read preserved actin as evidence against actin disruptors, when it is consistent with dose progression.

Lookup e21/e22 confirmed name and BBBC021 structure agree for cytochalasin B but provided no curated mechanisms to rescue the inference, and literature search on actin disruptor multinucleation tubulin phenotype returned 0 hits e24, leaving me without orthogonal context.

Lesson: when actin texture is the strongest high-dose feature and atlas is 0/10 for the top call with conflicting microscopist calls across doses, a strong tubulin intensity dose-response should be down-weighted as secondary to cell contraction, and probability should stay near 0.25 or lower without replicate wells or a tubulin polymerization / actin filament direct assay.

What was right:
- e3 act_glcm_contrast z=+36 > tub_mean +27.7 and e6 Actin disruptors call at high dose
- e4/e10 multinucleation dose-dependent rho +1.00 is consistent with actin cytokinesis failure PMID 8204105
- e8 atlas 0/10 stabilizer neighbours contradicted my call
- e14 flat cell_count and persistent nuc_area/solidity -1.00 trends argued against stabilizer arrest

What was wrong or missed:
- misinterpreted tub_mean +6.6 to +27.7 dose_response as stabilizer polymerization not compaction artifact from cell_area -7.2 to -8.4
- overconfident p=0.47-0.38 on single well per dose with rho= +/-1.00 n=4
- discounted e6 Actin and e7 Aurora alternatives and e8 atlas
- e18 early preserved actin misread as against actin disruptor

Proposed next experiment: High-resolution actin/tubulin co-stain with replicates at 0.3, 1, 10 uM vs latrunculin B control plus in vitro tubulin polymerization assay; quantify actin fibre loss and tubulin bundles independently of cell area normalization.
